Release notes/v0.6.1/Oct 19, 2026

What's new in Cadence 0.6.1.

Cadence now aims higher when it picks your next work: goals read as where you're taking each project, and proposals are real steps toward them that an agent can carry for hours, not small chores.

By Cadence Labs · Filed in Releases

§01 Changed

  • Goals are outcomes. Each project's goal now says who it's for, what changes, and how far you're taking it, with a "done when" you can check. Draft again in Your judgment redrafts them from all your work; goals you've changed stay as you wrote them. Learning from your past sessions redrafts the ones Cadence drafted.
  • Milestones. Proposals marked milestone are the biggest step toward a goal one agent can carry on its own branch: it plans first, works through it, and commits at each step. Smaller next steps still come when you've asked for something specific.
  • More to choose from. Cadence looks at each project on its own and keeps up to three proposals waiting per project, each still quoting where it came from.

§02 Fixed

  • Proposals for most projects were being dropped before you saw them.
  • After learning from past sessions, Cadence could read your recent work out of order.
